extracted.intended_audience: general public; stakeholders, researchers and participants interested in the Productivity Commission and its public inquiry processes
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Productivity Commission's functions, operating principles and procedural requirements for studies and public inquiries, including how inquiries are commissioned, run, and how public input is handled. Useful for people preparing submissions or engaging with PC inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to Treasurer references (commissioned studies and inquiries)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PC operates within the Treasury portfolio and its core function involves responding to references from the Treasurer, which can request a commissioned study or a public inquiry. References to the PC stipulate the length and terms of the project and may cover any sector of the Australian economy; address a particular industry or cut across industry boundaries; and involve wider social or environmental issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most projects are specified for nine or twelve-month duration, although some may be six or fifteen months. References set the scope, length and terms of work the PC will undertake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of submissions and formal public consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Both studies and inquiries accept submissions from members of the public, although inquiries are additionally required (under the Act) to undertake formal public consultations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processes provide for extensive public input and feedback through hearings, workshops and other consultative forums, and through the release of draft reports and preliminary findings. All reports are publicly released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of advice and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission's advice to government, and the information and analysis on which it is based, are open to public scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency is implemented via public consultations, hearings, workshops, the release of draft reports and preliminary findings, and public release of final reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence in findings and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission operates under the protection and guidelines of its own legislation and has an arm's length relationship with the Government. While the Government largely determines its work program, it cannot tell it what to say and the commission's findings and recommendations are based on its own analyses and judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence means the PC's outputs reflect its analysis rather than direction from government; this underpins the credibility of its reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-wide focus (statutory obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission is obliged under its statutory guidelines to take a broad view, encompassing the interests of the economy and community as a whole, rather than just particular industries or groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environmental, regional and social dimensions of its work are also considered, informed by public consultation and the commission's own research capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner appointment criteria and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The PC is headed by a Chair and between 4 and 12 other Commissioners, who are appointed for a five year term on the advice of the Treasurer. Some commissioners are required to have particular skills and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified desirable skills and experience include: (a) applying the principles of ecologically sustainable development and environmental conservation; (b) dealing with the social effects of economic adjustment and social welfare service delivery; (c) experience in working in Australian industry; (d) dealing with policies and programs that impact Indigenous persons and communities. Associate Commissioners can be appointed on a full or part-time basis; PC staff are Commonwealth public servants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabling requirement for final inquiry reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Final inquiry reports must be tabled in Parliament within 25 sitting days of the Government receiving the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PC reports formally through the Treasurer to the Australian Parliament, where its inquiry reports are tabled; this is a statutory procedural deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional statutory roles and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: The PC acts as the secretariat to the intergovernmental Review of Government Service Provision, produces annually the Report on Government Services, and issues regular reports on the effectiveness of government services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission can also undertake Commission-initiated research and operates as the Australian Government's competitive neutrality complaints mechanism; these roles shape the range of outputs stakeholders might engage with.
